content:
Apple TV has so far completely steered clear of the hit reality dating show genre. While its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "docuseries" rather than a "reality show," this is still the streamer's first dating show.

"The Last Person on Earth" features renowned relationship therapist Esther Perel, who will be conducting an "innovative experiment"

Esther Perel is a famous relationship therapist and a New York Times bestselling author, specializing in the field of interpersonal relationships.

Perel is also the central figure of Apple TV's newly announced 8-episode dating docuseries "The Last Person on Earth".

According to the press release: "In the series, seemingly opposite-in-personality couples will be meticulously matched by Perel and a team of matchmaking experts and therapists, before embarking on adventures to the world's most romantic and remote destinations."

It sounds exactly like a reality show, just avoiding the negative baggage that comes with that reality show brand. My guess is that Apple wanted to give its dating show an "upscale" feel, hence the "docuseries" label.

Here is Perel herself introducing the show:

The series has not yet announced a release date, but is expected to premiere in 2027.

Speaking of which, Apple announced yesterday that it will adapt the latest romance novel by bestselling author Rebecca Yarros into a TV series. Clearly, the streamer wants to expand its existing core genres, going beyond its current sci-fi, comedy, and thriller offerings.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, and is also available through the Apple One bundle.
